framework.summary: The bill requires developers to write no safety framework; the Energy Secretary develops containment recommendations.

transparency_report.summary: Developers must publish nothing; test reports go privately to each participant and the Secretary reports to Congress.

incident_reporting.summary: The bill requires developers to report no incidents to government.

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: The bill sets no imminent-risk reporting window.

third_party_audit.summary: The Energy Secretary, through the National Laboratories, tests AI and must facilitate third-party assessments where practicable; developers need not commission an independent audit.
third_party_audit.quote: Facilitate to the extent practicable independent, third-party assessments and blind model evaluations of such artificial intelligence.

whistleblower.summary: The bill has no whistleblower protections.

registration.summary: No registration or licensing; developers must only take part in the federal testing program.

shutdown.summary: The bill requires no shutdown or kill-switch capability; it only has the Secretary recommend containment protocols.

compute_threshold.summary: Advanced AI means AI trained with more than 10^26 operations, or another amount the Secretary sets by rule.
compute_threshold.quote: Artificial intelligence trained utilizing a quantity of computing power greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations

revenue_threshold.summary: A large developer must have spent at least $2,000,000,000, with affiliates, on developing or modifying AI over the prior five calendar years.
revenue_threshold.quote: not less than $2,000,000,000 on investments to develop or modify artificial intelligence

harm_threshold.summary: A loss-of-control scenario means AI behavior causing at least 5 deaths, serious injury to at least 50 people, or more than $100,000,000 in damages.
harm_threshold.quote: results in the death of not fewer than five individuals, serious bodily injury to not fewer than 50 individuals, or more than $100,000,000 in damages.

penalties.summary: The Energy Secretary may assess civil penalties up to $1 million per violation, each continuing day a separate violation; may subpoena model weights; the Attorney General may sue.
penalties.quote: the Secretary may assess on such developer a civil penalty of not more than $1 million for such violation.

effective_date.summary: The bill states no effective date; the Program must be set up within 90 days of enactment.

notes: Program-style bill (federal testing program, terminates 7 years after enactment). Duties on developers are participation and access (including model weights); registration marked partial for that reason, reviewer may prefer not_in_bill.
